spheroid_closest — DRIVE diabolo op

• Data kinds: signal × table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.spheroid_closest(x, sph: 'dict') -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import diabolo; diabolo.spheroid_closest(x, sph: 'dict') -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("spheroid_closest"))

Usage

Point x → closest point on the spheroid surface point, signed distance s (> 0 inside, the paper's definition of s) and outward unit normal normal (direction of the gradient at the closest point).

The closest point uses Eberly's bisection on the ellipse in the meridian plane. ★The public implementation shrinks radially from the centre and returns that point (not the closest point; for a point 5 mm outside the ellipsoid it differs by up to 2.2 mm), and approximates the normal by (x/b, y/a, z/b) (the gradient would use squares; off the axes it deviates by up to 12.2°). Here it is written as in the paper's text, "move to the closest point", with the true normal. Raises ValueError: x is not a finite 3-vector, sph is not an ellipsoid dict.
